The sequence number we store in the sequence id is the last one we received
from the client.  So on the next operation we'll check that the client gives
us the next higher number.
We increment sequence id's at the last moment
of knowing the right error return.  (The decision to increment the sequence id
depends on the exact error returned.)
However on the *first* use of a sequence number
column2: if we set the sequence number

column1: to the one received from the client and then let the increment happen on
encode
column2: we'll be left with a sequence number one to high.

column1: For that reason
column2: ENCODE_SEQID_OP_TAIL only increments the sequence id on

column1: *confirmed* stateowners.
This creates a problem for open reclaims
column2: which are confirmed on first use.

column1: Therefore the open reclaim code
sequence id
column2: cancelling out the undesired increment on encode.  But this

column1: prevents the sequence id from ever being incremented in the case where
multiple reclaims are sent with the same openowner.  Yuch!
We could add another exception to the open reclaim code
sequence id only if this is the first use of the open owner.
But it's simpler by far to modify the meaning of the op_seqid field: instead
of representing the previous value sent by the client
encoding
column2: to represent the *next* sequence id that we expect from the client.

column1: This eliminates the need for special-case handling of the first use of a
stateowner.
